title: How To Create and Sell All-Over Print Products
summary: All-over prints cover the entire surface of a garment or product. Find out the technical and practical details to design and sell AOP products.
body_markdown:
All-over print (AOP) is a design that covers a product’s entire fabric surface. Items like sweatshirts, T-shirts, leggings, and tote bags with AOP have artwork from seam to seam, compared to other forms of fabric printing that feature a contained image or pattern on one or two panels or sections.


Dye sublimation, the printing technique behind most all-over print items, is a growing market.[Mordor Intelligence](https://www.mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/dye-sublimation-printing-market) projects that the dye-sublimation printing market will grow from $16.85 billion in 2026 to $28.05 billion by 2031, a 10.72% compound annual growth rate (CAGR). It also reports that garments made up 62.31% of 2025 dye sublimation printing revenue.


In a[print-on-demand (POD)](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/dropshipping/recommended-dropshipping-and-pod-apps) model, AOP products are made and shipped only after a customer places an order. This guide explains what the all-over printing process is, how it works, and how to create and sell all-over print-on-demand apparel with the help of POD apps.


## What is the all-over print process?


All-over print is a printing technique that covers an entire garment or fabric item, including sleeves and seams, with one design.[Printful](https://www.printful.com/all-over-print) , a popular choice for all-over print shirts, says that’s what sets AOP apart from[direct-to-garment (DTG) printing](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-dtg-printing) methods, which cover only one flat area. Because the fabric is printed before being cut and sewn into the finished product, the all-over printing method is also called cut-and-sew printing.


Common all-over print products include:


-


**Apparel.** Such as T-shirts, hoodies, leggings, windbreakers, dresses, activewear, and swimwear.


-


**Accessories.** Such as hats, bags, and hair accessories.


-


**Home goods.** Such as blankets, pillows, and flags.


All-over print works as both a creative technique and an online business opportunity. As a technique, it provides access to eye-catching designs, vibrant colors, wraparound graphics, and a larger canvas on your products.


Many POD vendors can print custom AOP designs without minimum order requirements, so you can test your all-over print design one order at a time.


## How all-over printing works with POD suppliers


Here are the basic steps in the AOP process (when using a POD service). Suppliers use sublimation printing for synthetic fabrics and direct-to-fabric printing for cotton:


1. **Prepare the artwork.** Size the design to the product template and use a full-bleed image, or one that extends to every edge of the template.


2. **Print the design.** For synthetic fabric, the POD service prints the design on sublimation transfer paper. For natural fabrics like cotton, they print directly on the fabric using water-based inks.


3. **Transfer the design.** For synthetics, a heat press moves the design from the paper to the fabric. This step isn’t needed for cotton printing because the graphic is printed directly on the fabric.


4. **Cut the fabric.** The POD service cuts the printed fabric into panels that match your product’s layout.


5. **Sew the product.** The panels are sewn into the finished product.


6. **Ship the order.** The supplier ships the final product to your customer under your brand.

### How sublimation printing works


[Sublimation printing](https://www.shopify.com/blog/sublimation-printing) uses heat, pressure, and time to turn solid dye into a gas that bonds with the material. Because the dye becomes part of the fiber instead of sitting on top of it, the print resists cracking and peeling and retains its color through multiple washes.


The sublimation process has limits. It works only on polyester or polymer-coated surfaces, including high-polyester blends, and it’s available only on white or very light products because standard sublimation printers don’t print white. Lower polyester content can also fade the print.


### All-over print vs. DTG


[DTG](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-dtg-printing) uses a digital printer to print a design directly onto a finished garment, usually cotton. DTG and AOP are both popular in the made-to-order garment industry. Both are digital processes with quick setup, and both embed ink into the fabric instead of layering it on top. They differ in materials, colors, and coverage:


**** **All-over print products** **DTG products**


**Recommended materials** Polyester and high-polyester blends 100% cotton and high-cotton fabrics


**Fabric colors** White or very light only Any color (dark garments need a white underbase)


**Print areas** Seam-to-seam Limited by the printer’s platen—the flat board that holds the garment on while it prints


**Durability** Dye becomes part of the polyester fiber Pigment can gradually lighten over many washes


**Finishing** Print, transfer, cut, and sew Prints directly onto a finished garment


### When screen printing makes sense


You can also explore a third option for print-on-demand fabric items:[screen printing](https://www.shopify.com/blog/heat-press-vs-screen-printing) . When you print tees and other fabric items via screen printing, you’re pushing ink through a screen onto the product, with a separate screen to layer on each color. Screen printing works particularly well on cotton items, and it’s more cost-effective at higher volumes, as the setup cost is spread across more units.


Screen printing prints a set area rather than seam to seam, making it well-suited to large runs of simple, few-color designs, such as uniforms and promotional wear, rather than detailed all-over patterns.


## How to create and sell all-over print products


1. Develop distinctive designs
2. Choose a supplier for a small initial run
3. Price your products
4. Market your products
5. Fulfill orders and review the results


Here’s a step-by-step guide to creating and selling POD products.


### 1. Develop distinctive designs


Create an original design sized to your supplier’s template, and aim to distinguish your design from available products on the market. “Find your point of differentiation and go for it,” Morgan Cros, founder of[Original Duckhead](https://originalduckhead.com/?srsltid=AU7gw4VnDrjEPWX299xV2Vy_GJ25wKtH2afX5BeBMxJf33SbbF4QS8Z2) , says on *[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/original-duckhead-retail-strategy-breaking-into-the-market)* . You can also team up with outside creators, as Morgan does. “We regularly work with independent brands or designers just to inject that newness and that excitement for the brand,” she says.


Image file requirements vary by supplier. For example, Printful’s artwork guidelines instruct users to upload PNG or JPG files of at least 150 dpi in the sRGB color profile, where the bleed area covers the entire template.


### 2. Choose a supplier for a small initial run


Install a[POD app](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/dropshipping/recommended-dropshipping-and-pod-apps) , such as[Printful](https://apps.shopify.com/printful) or[Gelato](https://apps.shopify.com/gelato-print-on-demand) , for your online store. Before committing, confirm that your chosen app can handle all-over print or sublimation products, then place a few[test orders](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/dropshipping/creating-a-product-line/choosing-suppliers) to check shipping speed and packing quality.


Launch with a small set of products rather than your full catalog. Match products to the process (for example, adhering to sublimation printing’s need for polyester and white or very light-colored items), then let sales guide the next collection.


Mary Gui, founder of[Sock Candy](https://sockcandy.com/?srsltid=AU7gw4XIhrhwskRNEmwrediBadrCcydgZCG4GWVEHlzMSQGzfB4dzivp) , launched with seven cotton styles and three sheer styles. “Immediately the sheer styles started selling way faster than the cotton styles,” Mary says on[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/sock-candy-reddit-and-creative-marketing-tips) , so the next collection flipped the ratio. Because many POD apps have no minimums, you can run a similar small test without buying stock.


### 3. Price your products


Find each product’s base cost in the POD app, set a retail price that covers it with room for profit, then sync the products to your store. Teri Johnson, founder of[Harlem Candle Company](https://www.harlemcandleco.com/?srsltid=AU7gw4Xq0JZDlxVQ1TpXrueRtHwMGOaHbwzfF_FfWu28qJ8ms1raAKOc) , advises entrepreneurs to hold off on pricing until they have a clear picture of their input costs. “Always know what your cost of goods are and what is the maximum that they ever should be,” Teri says on[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/harlem-candle-co-scent-of-success) .


Your input costs are part of your overall[cost of goods sold (COGS)](https://www.shopify.com/blog/cost-of-goods-sold) and[cost of goods manufactured (COGM)](https://www.shopify.com/blog/cost-of-goods-manufactured) —two metrics that help sellers monitor expenses and hit their desired[profit margin](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-profit-margin) . Shopify has an easy-to-use[profit margin calculator](https://www.shopify.com/tools/profit-margin-calculator) you can use once you know your input costs.


### 4. Market your products


Show your products in use, such as on models or styled with other items, and track what each marketing dollar returns. Original Duckhead’s Morgan Cros says customers told her team they needed to see the product in use, so the brand started adding lifestyle photos in addition to product photos.


Mary Gui says Sock Candy stands apart by styling its socks with different footwear and clothing as a complete look, rather than showing photos of the socks against white backgrounds.


Marketing can be a big expense, so it’s essential to work with a detailed plan. Maurice Mosseri, cofounder of[Still Here](https://www.stillhere.nyc/collections/all?srsltid=AU7gw4XSlduhSc2pgaWd4_4TRtBBMo_eJ6mAbFL-FWl0rjk4pP4UUGaK) , says early marketing spend needed an accountable return. “If we were spending a thousand dollars, that had to come back as $2,000 or more,” Maurice tells[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/still-here-fashioning-success) . Shopify has a[ROAS calculator](https://www.shopify.com/blog/how-to-calculate-roas) , which is an easy way to compute your[return on ad spend](https://www.shopify.com/blog/roas) .


### 5. Fulfill orders and review the results


When an order comes in, your supplier prints and ships it. As the person who made the sale and the keeper of the customer relationship, track which designs sell and how reliably the supplier delivers.


[Life is Good](https://lifeisgood.com/?srsltid=AU7gw4XhU81bvFRHFRZFCCwZwH_aI0wQfuPj5P3MXSbLAxvdZFoQCr_M) , which prints on demand, lists new graphics before any are made. President Tom Hassell says on[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/life-is-good-optimism-on-demand) that a new graphic can go online “as a virtual item, and doesn’t actually exist until after the customer places the order.” Armed with sales data, Tom says he can “know within a day or two which ones are resonating.”


Monitor reviews and other forms of customer feedback, as they’ll tell you a lot about your supplier. Are your T-shirts soft? Do the designs come out right every single time, or are there errors like white streaks? Does the image cover the entire fabric edge to edge? Can the supplier handle bulk orders and deliver in a reasonable shipping time? If you or your customers aren’t satisfied, consider switching suppliers.


## All-over print FAQ


### What does all-over print mean?


All-over print is a technique that covers the entire surface of a product with a design, including sleeves and seams, instead of a single print area. It’s a way to get your detailed, high-resolution artwork onto the maximum surface area of apparel and fabric accessories.


### Is DTF better on cotton or polyester?


Direct to film (DTF) works on both cotton and polyester. In the DTF process, a machine prints a design onto film, then transfers it to the garment with heat and adhesive. Popular print-on-demand platform[Printful says](https://www.printful.com/direct-to-film-printing) DTF “works better on a wider range of fabrics, including polyester and blends,” while DTG “is best suited for cotton.” DTF prints a set area, so it doesn’t give all-over coverage. To get all-over coverage on cotton, some suppliers print directly onto the fabric before it’s cut and sewn.


### Which print-on-demand service is best for all-over print?


Choosing the best POD service for all-over print will depend on your products, fabrics, and shipping needs. Shopify sellers can start with the platform’s[recommended POD apps](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/dropshipping/recommended-dropshipping-and-pod-apps) , which include Printful and Gelato. From there, you can filter each catalog for all-over print or sublimation products, compare pricing and shipping, and order samples before you commit.
